practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Test should focus on a single behavior. EVALUATION: The method performs one Act (new Grafo()) and then asserts properties of that single action. DECISION: only one distinct method call is tested and assertions relate to that behavior. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should not share mutable state or depend on order. EVALUATION: The test uses only local variables and no @Before/@After are required. DECISION: no static/instance state visible; test uses local variables only. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Need at least a happy path and an error scenario. EVALUATION: The class contains a single test method covering only the happy path; no exception tests (@Test(expected)/assertThrows) and fewer than 2 test methods. DECISION: class has <2 tests and only happy path present. VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Test boundary values when input domains exist. EVALUATION: This test constructs an object via the no-arg constructor; there are no obvious numeric/string input boundaries in the method under test. DECISION: boundary analysis not relevant to default constructor invocation. VERDICT: not-applicable.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained and avoid duplication. EVALUATION: Single short test is self-contained and there is no duplicated code across methods visible. DECISION: no helper methods required given single test; short and modular. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Keep tests small and simple. EVALUATION: The method is short, linear, contains no loops or conditionals and low cyclomatic complexity. DECISION: meets size and complexity thresholds. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should verify multiple properties. EVALUATION: The test uses three assertions checking existence, type and toString result, verifying multiple properties of the created object. DECISION: >=2 meaningful assertions present. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Avoid @Ignore/@Disabled and commented-out tests. EVALUATION: No @Ignore/@Disabled, no commented-out @Test or TODOs in the provided snippet. DECISION: tests are active and runnable. VERDICT: compliant.
PRINCIPLE: Tests should reference requirements. EVALUATION: Method Javadoc explicitly states 'Tests REQ-001' and requirement details. DECISION: traceability present in Javadoc. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Performance/security tests are separate concerns. EVALUATION: No timing or security tests detected; for a unit test of a constructor this is typically not relevant. DECISION: mark as not-applicable for this unit test. VERDICT: not-applicable.

PRINCIPLE: Test names should describe scenario and expected outcome. EVALUATION: The method name is 'test0', which is generic and does not describe scenario or expected result. DECISION: generic naming triggers non-compliance. VERDICT: non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Avoid heavy auto-generated verbose tests. EVALUATION: The class uses EvoSuite / EvoRunner (annotations and imports) and a generic test name 'test0' which are signs of generated tests. DECISION: presence of EvoSuite/EvoRunner annotations and generic naming indicates heavy generation. VERDICT: non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should show thoughtful design (Given-When-Then). EVALUATION: The method contains Given-When-Then comments and Javadoc describing the requirement; this indicates BDD-like intent. DECISION: Given-When-Then comments exist. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on public API and avoid implementation internals. EVALUATION: Test uses public constructor and public toString(); no reflection or internal state access. DECISION: interacts only with public API. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Use clear and specific assertions with messages. EVALUATION: Assertions use assertNotNull and assertTrue with descriptive messages; multiple assertions verify different properties. DECISION: assertions are specific and include messages. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Comments should explain 'why', not 'what'. EVALUATION: The test includes brief Given-When-Then comments and useful Javadoc; no commented-out code or excessive inline comments. DECISION: comments are minimal and valuable. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must avoid non-deterministic sources. EVALUATION: No Random, time-based calls, Thread.sleep, or external dependencies are used in the method. DECISION: deterministic behavior observed. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should not modify shared state or require cleanup. EVALUATION: Only local object creation is present and no external resources are used; no cleanup required. DECISION: side-effect free. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Use @Tag/@Category to organize tests. EVALUATION: There are no labeling annotations and the class contains only one test. DECISION: for a single-test class this practice is of limited applicability; mark as not-applicable. VERDICT: not-applicable.

practices_report.description: Each test case must focus on a single requirement or behavior.
Test cases should not depend on other tests or on execution order.

practices_report.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_report.description: Test cases must check both normal and edge case scenarios.
Tests should validate inputs at minimum, maximum, and just outside boundaries.
Tests should be self-contained and reusable; extract repeated setup into helpers.

practices_report.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_report.description: Keep test cases small and focused; avoid unnecessary complexity.
Assertions should be comprehensive and verify all relevant properties.
Avoid @Ignore or commented-out tests; keep the suite active.
Each test should be linked to a requirement.

practices_report.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_report.description: Performance and security must be tested separately from functional tests.
Test names should describe the scenario and expected outcome.

practices_report.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_report.description: Generated test code should be minimal and focused.

practices_report.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_report.description: Prioritize tests and use Given-When-Then structure when possible.

practices_report.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_report.description: Focus tests on observable behavior through public APIs, not internals.
Use specific assertions with descriptive messages where appropriate.
Comments should explain 'why' and be minimal.
